newsitem.title: UK: Europe, inland phones and mobile helped BT.
newsitem.headline: Europe, inland phones and mobile helped BT.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday that the main areas of growth in its first half were its European operations, inland telephone calls and mobile communications.
The value of price reductions exceeded 300 million stg in the half year, the company said in its second quarter and first half results statement.

Cellnet, the mobile telephone business which is 60/40 percent held by BT and Securicor, increased its customer base by 154,000 in the half year, bringing the total to over 2.5 million, including 654,000 digital connections.
Mobile communications turnover rose by 13.7 percent in the half year. Increasing competition and price cuts earlier in the year had dampened turnover growth rates, BT said.

BT said its Concert services, a joint operation with America's MCI Communications to provide seamless communications services to big business customers, were increasing in demand in Europe and turnover was growing rapidly.
Inland call volume growth rose to over seven percent on a twelve-month moving average basis, stimulated by price cuts and marketing initiatives. Inland call turnover rose 2.7 percent.

However, sharp price cuts and stiff competition triggered a 4.6 percent fall in international telephone call turnover in the half year. Volume growth on a 12 month moving average basis remained flat at eight percent.

BT, which earlier posted a 2.0 million stg fall in second quarter pretax profits to 730 million stg, also said it had kept hold of its 20.5 million residential lines in the 12 month period despite increased competition.
